title: Intersection bounds for affine half-intervals over finite fields
statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be a finite field, and for $t\neq 0$ define

$$
S_n(s,t)=\{s+it\mid i\in[1,(n+1)/2]\}.
$$

For two such sets, multiplication by $t_1^{-1}$ and translation by $-s_1$ reduce their intersection to $S_n(0,1)\cap S_n(s_2-s_1,t_1^{-1}t_2)$.

**Intersection-bound conjecture.** If $t_1^{-1}t_2\notin\{1,n-1\}$, then

$$
|S_n(s_1,t_1)\cap S_n(s_2,t_2)|\leq\left\lceil\frac{n}{3}\right\rceil
$$

for all $s_1,s_2$. Moreover, if $t_1^{-1}t_2\notin\langle\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,\dots,\pm k\}\rangle$, then

$$
|S_n(s_1,t_1)\cap S_n(s_2,t_2)|\leq\left\lceil\frac{(k+1)n}{2(2k+1)}\right\rceil
$$

for all $s_1,s_2$.

These bounds are intended to control overlaps among the edge sets used in two-star-tree codes and could yield constructions less dependent on the parameter $m$. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution status, so the claim remains open.
source_name: Yanzhi Li, Wenjie Zhong, Tingting Chen and Xiande Zhang, “Improved Bounds for Codes over Trees”, arXiv:2504.06556 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06556

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).
